newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: AMPLATS SEES 1997 SURPLUS DOWN, GOOD DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: AMPLATS SEES 1997 SURPLUS DOWN, GOOD DEMAND.

text.p: Anglo American Platinum Corp (Amplats) of South Africa Ltd said on Tuesday it expected a reduced world platinum surplus of 65,000 ounces in 1997 from 80,000 in 1996 and predicted growing demand for the precious metal into the next century.
Managing director Barry Davison told a presentation that demand should grow by around two percent a year until at least 2010.
"The platinum business will fundamentally remain good business over that period. We hopefully expect growth in volume demand of two percent per annum," he said.
"It certainly provides us with opportunities on the marketing side."
An expected drop in Russian supplies as stockpiles were depleted would help reduce the surplus of supply over demand this year, he predicted.
Amplats expects 1997 supply to total 4.963 million oz against demand of 4.898 million oz, compared to supply of 4.850 million oz in 1996 and demand of 4.770 million.

The company earlier announced a major expansion of its operations with a new platinum mine at Boschkoppie in the Rustenburg area of South Africa and expansion of concentrator capacity at Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd .
